query: What company did Roscoe Channing form with the owner of a leading stable of thoroughbred racehorses?
ground_truth: Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Company

pipeline_result.response: Based on the provided context, Roscoe Channing formed a partnership with Cornelius Vanderbilt Whitney to create the Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Company in Flin Flon, Saskatchewan, Canada. Therefore, the company that Roscoe Channing formed with the owner of a leading stable of thoroughbred racehorses is the Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Company.
retrieved_context: Roscoe Channing: Roscoe H. Channing, Jr. (January 7, 1868 – April 1, 1961) was an All-American football player, member of the Rough Riders and mining executive.  Channing was an All-American halfback for Princeton University.  He was one of eleven players selected by Caspar Whitney for the first ever College Football All-America Team in 1889.  When the Spanish–American War commenced in 1898, Channing enlisted in Theodore Roosevelt's Rough Riders.  Roosevelt took pride in how many Ivy League football players enlisted in the Rough Riders.  Channing later went into the mining business and managed the mining operations of the Whitney family.  In the 1920s, he formed a partnership with his friend Cornelius Vanderbilt Whitney.  The two formed the Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Company in Flin Flon, Saskatchewan, Canada, and Channing served as the company's President.  Channing died in 1961.

Cornelius Vanderbilt Whitney: Cornelius Vanderbilt "C.V." ("Sonny") Whitney (February 20, 1899 – December 13, 1992) was an American businessman, film producer, writer, philanthropist, polo player, and government official, as well as the owner of a leading stable of thoroughbred racehorses.

Wilson Stakes: The Wilson Stakes/Handicap was an American Thoroughbred horse race run for twenty-nine years between 1930 and 1958.  Inaugurated at the Saratoga Race Course in Saratoga Springs, New York, it was named In honor of Richard Thornton Wilson, Jr., a prominent Thoroughbred owner and president of Saratoga Race Course.
